Wiktionary articles in the answer language (via kaikki.org); English words also from the translation tables of the English Wiktionary; WikDict where Wiktionary has no article. The first line: the word with its grammar and the main meanings.
Gender, plural, verb forms, irregular or strong — from Wiktionary\'s inflection tables. Every form leads to its word: Häusern → Haus, went → go. Only what Wiktionary says, no guessing.

Firefox Translations models (Mozilla), the best one for each direction, running on the device. Between two languages other than English it goes through English: the meaning comes through, nuances (formal you, gender) may get lost.
fastText (lid.176); when it is unsure (a word or two), the dictionary that knows more of the words decides.
Our scripts on GitHub build every pack from these open sources and check it with tests (words and their forms) before publishing; the app downloads only from the project\'s releases.

Any StarDict dictionary, the format KOReader, GoldenDict and ColorDict use: download one from WikDict, Wiktionary or FreeDict, import files, or point the app to a folder. In the card they come after the packs, each line signed with its name; their first meaning is shown as the short line.

Pick the dictionary\'s files together (.ifo, .idx or .idx.gz, .dict or .dict.dz, .syn if there is one) or one archive: zip, tar, tar.gz, tar.bz2, tar.xz, tar.zst. Every dictionary in it gets its own folder.
Other dictionaries are read from one folder, and downloads and imports go into it. Choose KOReader\'s (koreader/data/dict) and both apps share the same dictionaries; deleting one deletes it for both.
From the provider\'s list; free ones are marked.
An OpenAI-compatible server; for a home one change only the IP.
Only what each part asks for can be changed; the format stays. Saved answers are kept.
Each part is one key of the answer: its name stays, what to write there can change.
Answer language, brevity, formatting: for every request.
{lang} is the answer language. This text goes with every AI request.
A word: base form, gender, forms, meanings; a phrase: its translation.
The grammar of the selection and the words worth learning.
What it means here, nuances, three examples with a translation.
Optional tabs on top of the offline core: AI translation, Analysis and Context. Dictionary, grammar and offline translation never need it; with AI off its icons and tab are gone.
A word: its base form, gender, forms and main meanings; a phrase or passage: a natural translation that keeps the sentence type. Without a network Translate shows the offline translation.
Only the selected text goes to the provider you chose, with the answer language. Answers are kept on the device: a word looked up again opens offline.
Type the key here or put it into a file in InkPeek/keys (anthropic.key, openai.key, openrouter.key). The key never goes to logs, the screen or exports.
LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM and other servers with the OpenAI API: choose a preset and change the IP. No cloud, no key; the answer may take longer.
OpenRouter has free models: open the model list and tick «free only». Free models are slower and change often.
From an article back to the list or the word-by-word translation.
Grammar: which form it is, how it is built and the rule behind it. Words: the harder words, or synonyms and related ones.
Explanation: what it means here, register, idioms, nuances. Examples: three everyday sentences with a translation.
Import takes StarDict files (.ifo with its .idx and .dict or .dict.dz, picked together) or an archive with them.
A line, or part of an article, a translation or an AI answer: copy, share, search the web.
A pop-up dictionary and translator for e-book readers: language packs, your own StarDict dictionaries, offline translation; AI if you want it.
When settings open; one request to GitHub.
